newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Taiwan gives Gambia $7.2 mln to build road.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan gives Gambia $7.2 mln to build road.

text.p: Taiwan, pursuing its rivalry with China for diplomatic recognition in Africa, agreed on Saturday to give tiny Gambia $7.2 million to build a road, diplomats said.

Taiwan's ambassador Francis Chung Lee told reporters the grant, enshrined in an agreement signed on Saturday, would pay for an 80-km (50 miles) road between Essau and Kerewan with a bridge across the river from which Gambia takes its name.
Senegal's Compagnie Sahelienne d'Entreprise (CSE) will build the road and bridge.

Military coup leader Yahya Jammeh, who is running for president in September 26 elections, seized power in Gambia in 1994, alienating its Western aid partners. Taiwan has since been helping it with projects ranging from rice growing to farming and medicine.
After Chinese Nationalists lost their civil war against the Communists in 1949 and took refuge on Taiwan, Beijing considered the island a renegade province not entitled to international recognition.
Since many African countries won independence in the 1960s, China and Taiwan have wooed various governments in the world's poorest continent in a low-key struggle for their loyalty.
